newsitem.title: UK: S&P to assign bank ratings based on public info.
newsitem.headline: S&P to assign bank ratings based on public info.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it would expand its worldwide coverage of banks by assigning ratings based on public information.

S&P said it will assign roughly 250 new bank ratings, mostly in emerging markets, during the course of the next year. The first series of ratings on banks in Singapore, Indonesia, and the Philippines will be announced on November 25.

It said the new ratings, identified by a "pi" subscript, would employ similar analytical procedures to traditional credit ratings, but differ in that they were based on public disclosure and other sources of information.

"The pi ratings respond to market research, indicating a strong preference among counterparties and other market participants for Standard & Poor's AAA through D scale, which is a globally recognised benchmark of financial risk," S&P said in a statement.

S&P said it would announce ratings in December on Japanese regional banks, and institutions in Mexico, Colombia, and Slovakia. All ratings and the accompanying analyses are part of Standard & Poor's newly expanded BankRatings Service.

By explicitly identifying credit ratings based on public information with a pi subscript from its traditional ratings, S&P said it was differentiating its policies and products from those of other rating agencies.
